name: Question 1
problem: For the function $f(x,y,z)=2{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}-xy$, find a vector that's perpendicular to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(-2,-3,1).$
worked_solution:
A normal vector to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(-2,-3,1)$ can be found by computing 
$∇f(-2,-3,1).$ 

So, we first find the gradient and evaluate it at $(x,y,z)=(-2,-3,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\text{ }j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}-xy)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}-xy)\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(2{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}-xy)\,k \\  & =(4x-y)\text{ }i-x\text{ }j+2z\text{ }k \\ ∇f(-2,-3,1) & =(4(-2)-(-3))\,i-(-2)\,j+2(1)\,k \\  & =-5\,i+2\,j+2\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $-5\,i+2\,j+2\,k$ is perpendicular to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(-2,-3,1).$

Question 1
?

For the function f(x,y,z)=2x2+z2−xy, find a vector that's perpendicular to the level surface that passes through the point where (x,y,z)=(−2,−3,1).

a
2i−5j+2k
b
−5i+2j+2k
c
−2i−5j+2k
d
5i+2j+2k
e
−5i+2j−2k
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

A normal vector to the level surface that passes through the point where (x,y,z)=(−2,−3,1) can be found by computing ∇f(−2,−3,1).

So, we first find the gradient and evaluate it at (x,y,z)=(−2,−3,1):

∇f(x,y,z)=fx(x,y,z)i+fy(x,y,z) j+fz(x,y,z) k=∂∂x(2x2+z2−xy)i+∂∂y(2x2+z2−xy)j+∂∂z(2x2+z2−xy)k=(4x−y) i−x j+2z k∇f(−2,−3,1)=(4(−2)−(−3))i−(−2)j+2(1)k=−5i+2j+2k

Therefore, −5i+2j+2k is perpendicular to the level surface that passes through the point where (x,y,z)=(−2,−3,1).
